result.title: Intervention-Certified Amplification: A Validity Gate for $σ$-Weighted Post-Training
result.comment: 13 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Published in Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026; see https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-emnlp.2090/
result.summary: Hybrid post-training often mixes supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), using training-side signals to set each sample's balance. Such signals characterize the anchor data and policy, but not whether the emphasized behavior helps in the target task and evaluation setting. This mismatch can reactivate and amplify pretrained behavior even after its literal form is removed from supervision. We demonstrate this with DIAA (Dual-Implicit Adversarial Amplification), a per-sample $σ$-weighted SFT/RL hybrid. With all literal Python fences removed from its anchor, DIAA emits unexecuted Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR) on $29%$ of MATH-500 prompts, three times vanilla GRPO. Paired interventions show $10.6$ percentage points of accuracy recovery when TIR is suppressed and comparable contributions from SFT imitation and $σ$-amplification; a student trained on a $0%$-TIR teacher anchor emits it at $45.8%$. Intervention-Certified Amplification (ICA) gates $σ$ with paired-rollout target evidence. Frozen and online ICA reduce TIR to $13.8%$ and $11.2%$, halve residual drag, improve accuracy from $47.5%$ to $48.7%$ and $49.3%$, and transfer to held-out GSM8K without retuning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出按样本 σ 加权的 SFT/RL 混合后训练会依据训练侧信号放大预训练行为（如未被执行的 TIR），并用配对 rollout 的目标证据做门控，提出 ICA 以降低这种错误放大并提升准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「配对干预 + 目标侧证据门控」思路可能可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中贡献分配与监督信号是否真正作用于目标推理，但原文为纯文本数学推理，未涉及视觉或 latent 状态。
